source: ESPN injury reports, recorded by RIVL every few hours

3146557:hip.name: Jock Landale
3146557:hip.note: Landale is out for Wednesday's game against the Wizards with a left hip strain, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
3146557:hip.long: Landale is sidelined for a second consecutive game with the injury. Zuby Ejiofor should handle the No. 2 center spot for as long as Landale is on the shelf.

4701230:ankle.name: Jalen Johnson
4701230:ankle.note: Johnson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game in Washington, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
4701230:ankle.long: Johnson suffered a sprained left ankle in Saturday's 121-99 loss to New Orleans and was ruled out ahead of Monday's meeting with the Pacers. If Johnson can't get back on the floor Wednesday versus the Wizards, Luguentz Dort might make his second consecutive start.

4712863:foot.name: Mouhamed Gueye
4712863:foot.note: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
4712863:foot.long: Gueye will be re-evaluated by medical staff in 3-to-4 months, which means he'll miss all of training camp and preseason and likely the start of the 2026-27 regular season. It's a brutal blow for the fourth-year big man, given that the Hawks used the No. 23 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft to select St. John's product Zuby Ejiofor. Gueye's absence means Ejiofor will have more opportunities in the preseason, and the rookie could establish a key role off the bench behind Onyeka Okongwu and projected backup center Jock Landale (ankle).

5105571:knee.name: Henri Veesaar
5105571:knee.note: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
5105571:knee.long: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

4351852:rest.name: Mitchell Robinson
4351852:rest.note: Robinson (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic.
4351852:rest.long: Robinson has been downgraded from questionable to out and will miss the first half of Boston's upcoming back-to-back set. He'll likely be able to suit up Monday in Houston.

4433188:illness.name: Devin Carter
4433188:illness.note: Carter has been diagnosed with mononucleosis and is without a timetable for a return, Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reports.
4433188:illness.long: Carter missed Boston's final three preseason games with the illness and is now expected to miss time to begin the regular season. He can be considered week-to-week until Boston provides an update on his progress. The 2024 first-rounder signed a two-way pact with the Celtics on Saturday and will provide backcourt depth for the club.

5101761:rest.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
5101761:rest.note: Brown (rest) is out for Sunday's game in Indiana.
5101761:rest.long: Brown will skip the first leg of this upcoming back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game in New York. With Brown inactive, there will be more minutes available for Nolan Traore, Terance Mann and Keon Ellis.

5175643:leg.name: Egor Demin
5175643:leg.note: The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
5175643:leg.long: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.

5105626:shoulder.name: Tyler Bilodeau
5105626:shoulder.note: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
5105626:shoulder.long: Bilodeau will miss a third straight game to begin the regular season due to a right shoulder sprain. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

5061575:hamstring.name: Kon Knueppel
5061575:hamstring.note: Knueppel (hamstring) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
5061575:hamstring.long: Knueppel hasn't played this season, though it appears he will make his 2026-27 campaign debut versus Brooklyn. It may take him a few games to ramp up. However, Knueppel's return, even in a limited capacity, will presumably send Sion James back to the bench.

4395651:calf.name: Coby White
4395651:calf.note: White (calf) is probable for Wednesday's game in Brooklyn.
4395651:calf.long: White came out of his regular-season debut unscathed and should be available for Wednesday's game. White saw 16 minutes of action in Monday's 124-91 loss to the Pistons, but he should be cleared for more playing time in his second game of the season.

4066218:hamstring.name: Grant Williams
4066218:hamstring.note: Williams (hamstring) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Pistons.
4066218:hamstring.long: Williams has yet to suit up during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been much revealed about his health. However, until he is cleared to play, he should be considered week-to-week, meaning Royce O'Neale should see more minutes off the bench.

4684269:knee.name: Kylan Boswell
4684269:knee.note: Boswell (knee) is out for Wednesday's season opener against the Nets.
4684269:knee.long: Boswell continues to rehab after right knee surgery. The hope in early October was that he would be cleared for basketball activities prior to the start of the G League season, which begins in early November.

4848625:back.name: Dailyn Swain
4848625:back.note: Swain (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Boston.
4848625:back.long: Swain will be held out of Friday's contest due to lower-back soreness. His next chance to play will come Monday at Philadelphia.

4278067:hamstring.name: Nic Claxton
4278067:hamstring.note: Claxton (hamstring) is questionable for Wednesday against the Knicks.
4278067:hamstring.long: Claxton has now drawn his first questionable tag of the young season as he closes in on his debut. If he does get the green light, he may face restrictions early on. Jalen Smith (finger) and Zach Collins could lose some steam upon Claxton's return.

4683747:ankle.name: Jaylon Tyson
4683747:ankle.note: Tyson is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder due to a right ankle sprain.
4683747:ankle.long: Tyson is remaining sidelined for a third straight game due to the injury. Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja should continue to play meaningful roles for the Cavaliers until Tyson is ready to return.

5279129:knee.name: Sergio de Larrea
5279129:knee.note: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that de Larrea (knee) will be re-evaluated next week, Noah Weber of TheSmokingCuban.com reports.
5279129:knee.long: De Larrea sprained his right knee in Monday's win over Miami and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. However, his absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

4593125:knee.name: Santi Aldama
4593125:knee.note: Aldama (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
4593125:knee.long: The questionable tag is an upgrade for Aldama, who has either been listed as out or doubtful ahead of all of Dallas' games this season. If the 25-year-old is cleared to make his season debut following knee surgery, he'll likely operate under a minutes restriction.

5148538:heel.name: Tarik Biberovic
5148538:heel.note: Biberovic (heel) is listed as out for Monday's game against Sacramento.
5148538:heel.long: Biberovic has been battling inflammation in his right heel, preventing him from making his NBA debut. While the rookie should be considered week-to-week, he likely has a way to go before earning a meaningful role in Dallas even when he's cleared to suit up.

4683688:foot.name: Dereck Lively II
4683688:foot.note: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Kings.
4683688:foot.long: Although there haven't been any negative reports regarding Lively's rehab progress, it doesn't appear he will be back in the lineup anytime soon. For now, the 22-year-old should be considered week-to-week. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse should continue to handle most of the work at the five. Santi Aldama (knee) might also get involved in that area once he's cleared to return.

4065813:personal.name: Alpha Diallo
4065813:personal.note: Diallo (personal/wrist) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Phoenix, Vic Lombardi of Altitude Sports reports.
4065813:personal.long: Diallo will miss a fourth consecutive contest while attending to a personal matter. He's also dealing with a right wrist sprain. The 29-year-old's next opportunity to return to action will come Monday against the Trail Blazers.

4592427:hamstring.name: Spencer Jones
4592427:hamstring.note: Jones (hamstring) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Trail Blazers.
4592427:hamstring.long: Jones has yet to play during the 2026-27 campaign after suffering a hamstring injury during the preseason. He should be considered day-to-day, meaning his next opportunity to get on the floor will come Wednesday versus Toronto.

4432181:knee.name: Julian Strawther
4432181:knee.note: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
4432181:knee.long: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

4395702:hip.name: Isaiah Joe
4395702:hip.note: Joe (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Philadelphia.
4395702:hip.long: Joe will miss Wednesday's contest due to a right hip contusion, resulting in his fifth straight absence. This will continue to open up additional minutes on the perimeter for Detroit's reserves. Joe's next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Lakers.

4433621:hamstring.name: Jalen Duren
4433621:hamstring.note: Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
4433621:hamstring.long: Duren suffered the hamstring injury in Friday's win over Miami and is set to miss an extended period. Paul Reed is expected to join the starting five and carries significant fantasy value until Duren returns. John Collins and Tolu Smith are also candidates to see a bump in minutes in Duren's stead.

4997536:knee.name: Gui Santos
4997536:knee.note: Santos did not play in the second half of Sunday's 124-112 win over the Clippers due to a knee injury and will not play against the Suns on Monday, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
4997536:knee.long: Santos has been working through a knee injury that he picked up in preseason action in mid-October, and he was initially tagged as questionable for Sunday's game before being cleared to play. Head coach Steve Kerr told reporters after the game that the Warriors need "to get [Santos] right," so it's possible that the fifth-year forward is facing an extended absence beyond Monday's contest. Georges Niang and Al Horford both figure to see an uptick in playing time in Santos' absence.

6589:rest.name: Draymond Green
6589:rest.note: Green (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
6589:rest.long: Green will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game against the Suns. Graham Ike, Al Horford and Charles Bassey will help pick up the slack with Green inactive Sunday.

3975:rest.name: Stephen Curry
3975:rest.note: Curry (rest) won't play Sunday against the Clippers, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
3975:rest.long: Sunday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so Curry will receive a maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Suns. De'Anthony Melton could draw the start sans Curry, and Brandin Podziemski will be more involved in the offense.

3102531:illness.name: Kristaps Porzingis
3102531:illness.note: The Warriors are exploring potential trades involving Porzingis (personal), who remains away from the team indefinitely while dealing with ongoing health concerns, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
3102531:illness.long: Porzingis is reportedly contemplating his future in basketball as he continues to battle health issues that have plagued him for nearly two years. Golden State isn't expecting the veteran center to rejoin the team anytime soon, and his contract structure could make him an attractive trade piece despite the uncertainty surrounding his playing future. With no timetable for his return and retirement potentially on the table, Porzingis remains a highly speculative fantasy stash, even in leagues with injured reserve spots.

4432171:knee.name: Moses Moody
4432171:knee.note: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
4432171:knee.long: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

6430:knee.name: Jimmy Butler III
6430:knee.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
6430:knee.long: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

2991230:knee.name: Fred VanVleet
2991230:knee.note: VanVleet (knee) won't play Saturday against the Thunder.
2991230:knee.long: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so VanVleet will receive his standard maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Celtics. Reed Sheppard (back) is also out for Saturday's game, so Marcus Smart could draw the start at point guard, and Amen Thompson should see some increased playmaking responsibilities.

4711272:back.name: Reed Sheppard
4711272:back.note: Sheppard (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics.
4711272:back.long: Sheppard is in danger of missing his fourth game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Fred VanVleet (knee) not listed on the injury report, Marcus Smart could continue to be more involved than usual if Sheppard can't suit up Monday.

2991235:calf.name: Steven Adams
2991235:calf.note: Head coach Ime Udoka said Monday that Adams could be out "a week or two" due to his right soleus strain, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
2991235:calf.long: The veteran big man can be considered week-to-week until the Rockets offer another update on his status. In the meantime, Clint Capela will likely see increased playing time behind Alperen Sengun.

4017837:ankle.name: Ivica Zubac
4017837:ankle.note: Zubac (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hawks.
4017837:ankle.long: Zubac is slated to miss a fifth straight game due to an ankle sprain, and while the Pacers were optimistic about a quick return, it's fair to treat the big man as week-to-week, given he continues to be ruled out on the team's initial injury report. In the starting center's absence, Jay Huff and Larry Nance (illness) have handled increased roles.

4396909:hamstring.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:hamstring.note: Nesmith (hamstring) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against Brooklyn.
4396909:hamstring.long: Nesmith didn't play in the 123-120 loss to New Orleans on Opening Night but has played in each of the Pacers' last five contests. Although he could see limited action while he continues to work his way back from the left hamstring strain, he will likely be out there Sunday, barring a setback.

4278355:back.name: Obi Toppin
4278355:back.note: Toppin (back) is questionable for Monday's game against Atlanta.
4278355:back.long: Toppin remains day-to-day after missing the first leg of this back-to-back set. The Pacers could give him extended run if he's cleared to play with so many regulars sidelined.

2530530:hamstring.name: T.J. McConnell
2530530:hamstring.note: McConnell (hamstring) is out for Monday's game against the Hawks and remains week-to-week.
2530530:hamstring.long: There haven't been many updates on McConnell's progress, though he did practice with the Noblesville Boom on Saturday. Quenton Jackson is likely to see extended run in the meantime.

5157066:knee.name: Johnny Furphy
5157066:knee.note: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
5157066:knee.long: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

4433076:knee.name: Ben Sheppard
4433076:knee.note: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
4433076:knee.long: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

4396993:hamstring.name: Tyrese Haliburton
4396993:hamstring.note: Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least the next two weeks of action, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4396993:hamstring.long: Given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries, the Pacers will likely take their time bringing Haliburton back to the court, so don't be surprised if his absence extends beyond this two-week window. Andrew Nembhard (neck) and Pascal Siakam should each get a usage bump as they take over more of the playmaking duties sans Haliburton and there will be more minutes available for Quenton Jackson.

5108024:foot.name: Yanic Konan Niederhauser
5108024:foot.note: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser (foot) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
5108024:foot.long: Niederhauser remains unlikely to play a meaningful role in the short term following a seven-month recovery from foot surgery. The 23-year-old might instead make a phased return to action, possibly seeing limited minutes at some point in upcoming weeks and making some appearances in the G League. Last season, he averaged 4.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.3 assists per regular-season game during his rookie year.

4065778:foot.name: Max Strus
4065778:foot.note: Strus (foot) practiced and participated in 5-on-5 with the San Diego Clippers on Saturday, Los Angeles Clippers sideline reporter/host Ohm Youngmisuk reports.
4065778:foot.long: Strus continues to progress in his recovery from a partially torn plantar fascia in his right foot suffered in the Clippers' preseason opener. He'll keep working with the G League affiliate and will likely play his first minutes of the season there before he's cleared to return to the NBA level.

3913176:achilles.name: Brandon Ingram
3913176:achilles.note: The Clippers recalled Ingram (Achilles) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
3913176:achilles.long: Ingram appears to be making steady progress after missing the opening run of the 2026-27 season through a partial Achilles tear, although it remains unclear when he'll be an option again for the Clippers and how quickly he'll regain playing time. Having worked with the G League squad Sunday, the versatile man is back with the main team, and his eventual return to action will restore a major piece of the rotation. However, while Ingram remains out, Darius Garland and Kris Dunn look set to carry most of the workload in upcoming contests.

6580:knee.name: Bradley Beal
6580:knee.note: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
6580:knee.long: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

4396818:shoulder.name: Jordan Miller
4396818:shoulder.note: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
4396818:shoulder.long: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

4433137:foot.name: Ziaire Williams
4433137:foot.note: Williams (foot) is out for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
4433137:foot.long: Williams will now miss his third consecutive outing as he recovers from a left foot injury. Jake LaRavia is in line for a second straight start, while Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili should continue to see an uptick in minutes off the bench.

5060631:knee.name: Adou Thiero
5060631:knee.note: Head coach JJ Redick said Monday that Thiero (knee) has participated in live action, and the hope is that he'll be available by the end of the week, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
5060631:knee.long: Thiero has yet to make his season debut while recovering from a left knee injury, though he's trending in the right direction. However, the second-year forward isn't expected to play a meaningful role once healthy.

4593016:ankle.name: Quinten Post
4593016:ankle.note: Post (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
4593016:ankle.long: Post is set for a second consecutive absence while tending to a right ankle sprain. His next chance to return will arrive Wednesday against the Pacers.

4431785:back.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
4431785:back.note: Pippen (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
4431785:back.long: Pippen will miss a second consecutive contest due to lower-back soreness, with his next chance to suit up coming Wednesday against Indiana. Cam Spencer will likely see increased playing time off the bench with the 25-year-old sidelined.

4065733:back.name: Ty Jerome
4065733:back.note: Jerome (back) won't play in Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian.
4065733:back.long: Jerome has been battling a nagging back injury, though it will finally force him to miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Scotty Pippen (back) also sidelined, Cam Spencer is the favorite to start at the one.

3032976:back.name: Rudy Gobert
3032976:back.note: Gobert (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
3032976:back.long: Gobert will miss his first game of the season Saturday, which could result in Joan Beringer getting the start and Trey Lyles could see a bump in minutes. For now, Gobert should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Milwaukee.

4594268:knee.name: Anthony Edwards
4594268:knee.note: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
4594268:knee.long: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

3934673:achilles.name: Donte DiVincenzo
3934673:achilles.note: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
3934673:achilles.long: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

4277956:ankle.name: Jordan Poole
4277956:ankle.note: Poole (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Utah.
4277956:ankle.long: Poole is expected to return from a three-game layoff for the meeting with the Jazz on Wednesday. The 27-year-old hasn't had a memorable 2026-27 campaign thus far, averaging 6.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 steals across 16.0 minutes per contest. If Poole is cleared for action, it would likely mean fewer minutes for Bryce McGowens and Trendon Watford.

3907497:personal.name: Dejounte Murray
3907497:personal.note: Murray (personal) is out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
3907497:personal.long: Murray remains away from the team due to the birth of his son. His next opportunity to return will come Wednesday against the Jazz. Jeremiah Fears should be in line for another start at point guard with Murray and Jordan Poole (ankle) sidelined.

5061589:knee.name: Yves Missi
5061589:knee.note: Missi (knee) won't play in Saturday's game against Atlanta.
5061589:knee.long: Missi sustained a bone bruise in his left knee during the 120-119 loss to Utah on Oct. 23. The 22-year-old hasn't played since, and considering he doesn't have a definitive return date, he should be considered week-to-week. Without Missi on the floor, DeAndre Jordan, Derik Queen and Karlo Matkovic could all see more action, though it appears none of them are a lock to take over the interim starting center job at the moment.

4277869:ankle.name: Jose Alvarado
4277869:ankle.note: Alvarado (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against the Nets.
4277869:ankle.long: Alvarado has missed four straight games and was ruled out at least 24 hours in advance of each absence. However, it appears he's nearing a return to action. If available Monday, Alvarado would likely face limitations, while Jordan Clarkson and Tyler Kolek would be candidates for fewer minutes.

4683692:shoulder.name: Cason Wallace
4683692:shoulder.note: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
4683692:shoulder.long: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

4433255:knee.name: Chet Holmgren
4433255:knee.note: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
4433255:knee.long: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

4593803:leg.name: Jalen Williams
4593803:leg.note: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
4593803:leg.long: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

2991350:ankle.name: Alex Caruso
2991350:ankle.note: Caruso (ankle) is expected to miss time due to an ankle sprain, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
2991350:ankle.long: With Caruso already ruled out for Wednesday's game in Dallas due to an ankle sprain, it sounds like the veteran forward could remain sidelined beyond a one-game absence. That would leave Oklahoma City without one of its key rotation wings for at least the near term, which could force Jared McCain into a big role for the banged-up Thunder.

5061603:knee.name: Thomas Sorber
5061603:knee.note: Sorber (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
5061603:knee.long: Sorber remains in recovery mode due to knee surgery. Until the Thunder update his timetable for a return, Sorber can be deemed week-to-week.

5159925:back.name: Nikola Topic
5159925:back.note: Topic (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
5159925:back.long: Topic has yet to play during the 2026-27 campaign, and at this rate, it doesn't look like he will be on the floor anytime soon. For now, he should be considered week-to-week. The 2024 No. 12 overall pick has appeared in only 10 regular-season games throughout his career, averaging 5.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 4.4 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep over 16.0 minutes per contest.

4065654:knee.name: Jonathan Isaac
4065654:knee.note: Orlando recalled Isaac (knee) from the G League's Osceola Magic on Sunday.
4065654:knee.long: Isaac has been working on his rehabilitation from a significant knee injury and remains without a defined timeline to make his 2026-27 season debut. He was assigned to the G League club Sunday and recalled shortly after, presumably getting some practice with the affiliate team. Once he's healthy, Isaac could see minutes off the bench for Orlando.

4432165:knee.name: Jalen Suggs
4432165:knee.note: Suggs has been diagnosed with a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4432165:knee.long: Suggs suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Knicks when his right knee buckled following a layup attempt. Fortunately, further testing revealed no major structural damage, though the 25-year-old will miss at least two weeks before being re-evaluated. Anthony Black and Jase Richardson could see increased opportunities in Orlando's backcourt during Suggs' absence.

4432573:ankle.name: Paolo Banchero
4432573:ankle.note: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4432573:ankle.long: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

5214637:hamstring.name: Noah Penda
5214637:hamstring.note: Penda was diagnosed with a partially torn right hamstring Saturday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
5214637:hamstring.long: Penda suffered the hamstring tear in Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat. It's unknown how long the injury will keep the 21-year-old off the floor. However, since it's a different injury than the one he suffered in the same hamstring during training camp, the team may take a cautious approach regarding his return. Penda, the No. 32 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, averaged 3.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists over 12.8 minutes per outing in 59 regular-season games in 2025-26. While he's not expected to be a mainstay in the rotation throughout the 2026-27 campaign, his absence could open up a few minutes for Tristan Da Silva.

5107251:ankle.name: Izaiyah Nelson
5107251:ankle.note: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
5107251:ankle.long: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

3059318:foot.name: Joel Embiid
3059318:foot.note: Embiid (foot) is questionable to suit up for Monday's game against the Bulls.
3059318:foot.long: Embiid missed Saturday's 109-104 win over Charlotte due to right foot plantar fascia injury management, and he's now in jeopardy of missing a second consecutive game for the same reason. If he's unable to play Monday, Adem Bona will likely earn another start with Jabari Walker getting additional minutes off the bench.

1966:back.name: LeBron James
1966:back.note: James (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's meeting in Charlotte.
1966:back.long: James will rest on the second leg of a back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game against the Bulls. Dean Wade and Justin Edwards should see a bump in minutes with James inactive, while Tyrese Maxey figures to see a sizeable uptick in usage.

4870562:back.name: Dominick Barlow
4870562:back.note: Barlow (back) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Pistons, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
4870562:back.long: The 76ers were due to re-evaluate Barlow on Tuesday, but the big man remains in recovery mode ahead of Wednesday's action. Until the team updates his return timeline, Barlow can be considered week-to-week.

4871141:achilles.name: Ariel Hukporti
4871141:achilles.note: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
4871141:achilles.long: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

4701232:shoulder.name: Mark Williams
4701232:shoulder.note: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4701232:shoulder.long: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

4279888:hamstring.name: Ja Morant
4279888:hamstring.note: Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and is expected to miss four weeks, Portland announced Friday.
4279888:hamstring.long: Morant left Thursday's game early with a hamstring injury, which has since been revealed to be a strain that will result in a monthlong absence. The star guard leaves a major void in the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt, one that figures to be filled by Jrue Holiday for the foreseeable future.

4914336:knee.name: Shaedon Sharpe
4914336:knee.note: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
4914336:knee.long: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

4433174:calf.name: Dylan Cardwell
4433174:calf.note: Cardwell (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Mavericks.
4433174:calf.long: Cardwell was temporarily upgraded to probable ahead of Monday's clash, though he was downgraded twice before ultimately being ruled out with a left calf strain. His next chance to make his season debut will arrive Wednesday against the Lakers.

4898371:knee.name: Maxime Raynaud
4898371:knee.note: Raynaud (knee) is progressing in his rehabilitation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
4898371:knee.long: Raynaud's absence is expected to extend into mid-November due to a right patellar subluxation. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) set to miss at least one more week, Precious Achiuwa, Jonathan Mogbo and De'Andre Hunter are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

4594327:ankle.name: Keegan Murray
4594327:ankle.note: Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in 10-to-14 days, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
4594327:ankle.long: Murray has officially been diagnosed with left ankle capsulitis, and he's set to miss at least the next 10 days. Precious Achiuwa has been starting in Murray's absence, and he should continue to see opportunities along with De'Andre Hunter and Daeqwon Plowden.

3907387:achilles.name: Ben Simmons
3907387:achilles.note: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
3907387:achilles.long: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

6440:calf.name: Tobias Harris
6440:calf.note: Harris (calf) is listed as out for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
6440:calf.long: Harris suffered a strained left calf ahead of the 2026-27 campaign and has yet to make his debut with the Spurs. The veteran is slowly making progress toward a return, though he should be considered week-to-week until more information is released. The 34-year-old, who signed with San Antonio during the offseason, averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 27.7 minutes per contest in 63 regular-season appearances with the Pistons in 2025-26.

5101845:knee.name: Jayden Quaintance
5101845:knee.note: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
5101845:knee.long: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

6450:knee.name: Kawhi Leonard
6450:knee.note: Leonard (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least three to four weeks, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
6450:knee.long: The extended absence represents a significant setback for Leonard, who will be unavailable for the foreseeable future. His absence should create additional offensive opportunities for Toronto's remaining rotation players, with guys like RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes and Allen Graves seeing more usage. Leonard's recovery timeline will be worth monitoring, as the reported window represents a minimum absence rather than a firm return date.

4432586:foot.name: Nate Bittle
4432586:foot.note: Bittle (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Clippers and remains without a timetable to return.
4432586:foot.long: For now, fantasy managers can assume that he's week-to-week. He's not expected to crack the rotation upon his return.

4277961:knee.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
4277961:knee.note: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
4277961:knee.long: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

4433268:knee.name: Trey Alexander
4433268:knee.note: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
4433268:knee.long: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

3102530:foot.name: Jusuf Nurkic
3102530:foot.note: Nurkic (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
3102530:foot.long: Nurkic has been a spectator to begin the season, and he's still not ready for game action due to a foot injury. The veteran big man should be considered week-to-week until the Jazz update his recovery, so Jaxson Hayes should remain the team's primary center going forward.

4432907:foot.name: Justin Champagnie
4432907:foot.note: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
4432907:foot.long: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

4997537:hip.name: Tristan Vukcevic
4997537:hip.note: Vukcevic (hip) is listed as out for Monday's game against Orlando.
4997537:hip.long: The Wizards announced on Oct. 1 that Vukcevic would be sidelined for at least a month. However, there haven't been any definitive updates regarding when he will be able to get back on the floor. In the meantime, Deandre Ayton should see more minutes off the bench.

4606840:knee.name: Jamir Watkins
4606840:knee.note: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
4606840:knee.long: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

4397189:finger.name: Jalen Smith
4397189:finger.note: Smith is probable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks with a left finger sprain.
4397189:finger.long: Smith is expected to play through the injury Wednesday, but his time as Chicago's starting center could be coming to an end. Nic Claxton (hamstring) is questionable to make his season debut, and his return would send Smith into a bench role in all likelihood.

5105555:ankle.name: Tobe Awaka
5105555:ankle.note: Awaka (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
5105555:ankle.long: Awaka played 12 minutes during Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics after missing one game with the ankle issue. The rookie big man will continue to provide depth off the bench for the Bulls behind Jalen Smith.

4576087:hamstring.name: Peyton Watson
4576087:hamstring.note: Watson (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game in Oklahoma City.
4576087:hamstring.long: This will be Watson's second straight game on the sidelines, and with Friday's game being the first of a back-to-back set, he may need to spend an additional game on the inactive list. Meleek Thomas, Sam Merrill and Mario Hezonja will help pick up the slack in Watson's absence.

6442:knee.name: Kyrie Irving
6442:knee.note: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Kings.
6442:knee.long: Irving was initially listed as questionable before being downgraded to doubtful Monday afternoon, and he's since been ruled out. With the star floor general sidelined, Marcus Sasser and Walter Clayton are candidates for increased burn, while Cooper Flagg will likely see increased playmaking duties.

4065813:wrist.name: Alpha Diallo
4065813:wrist.note: Diallo (wrist) is listed as questionable for Monday's game versus Portland.
4065813:wrist.long: Diallo made his only appearance of the 2026-27 campaign in the 96-84 Opening Night loss to Oklahoma City. Since then, he has missed the Nuggets' last four games. While the personal issue that contributed to his absence has seemingly been resolved, a right wrist sprain may keep him off the floor for the fifth time this season.

3102529:ankle.name: Clint Capela
3102529:ankle.note: Capela (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves.
3102529:ankle.long: Capela is in danger of missing his second consecutive contest and third overall of the 2026-27 campaign. With Steven Adams (calf) sidelined, Jabari Smith may spend more time in the middle behind Alperen Sengun. Oscar Tshiebwe might also see a few minutes off the bench.

2528210:personal.name: Tim Hardaway Jr.
2528210:personal.note: Hardaway (personal) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers.
2528210:personal.long: Hardaway is dealing with a personal issue and is in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. If he can't suit up Monday in Los Angeles, Dru Smith and Nikola Jovic should see more minutes.

4397688:knee.name: Trey Murphy III
4397688:knee.note: Murphy (knee) is probable for Wednesday's game versus the Jazz.
4397688:knee.long: Murphy played through the knee issues and logged 40 minutes in Monday's 135-134 win over the Grizzlies, so it clearly didn't impact his playing time. It appears he'll continue to push through the pain Wednesday.

3064440:elbow.name: Zach LaVine
3064440:elbow.note: LaVine (elbow) is questionable to play in Monday's game against Dallas.
3064440:elbow.long: LaVine played a season-low 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis, but it's unclear if that was due to the elbow soreness or the game being out of reach for the Kings. Either way, his status will bear monitoring ahead of Monday's clash with the Mavericks. If he's unable to play, Darius Acuff Jr.'s usage would skyrocket, while Malik Monk, Emanuel Sharp and Nique Clifford could all see increased opportunities in the backcourt.

5160992:knee.name: Alex Sarr
5160992:knee.note: Sarr (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
5160992:knee.long: Sarr is dealing with left knee soreness that could force him to miss another contest after sitting out Monday's win over Orlando. If the big man remains sidelined, Deandre Ayton could continue to handle an increased workload in Washington's frontcourt. Sarr's availability should become clearer closer to Wednesday's tipoff.

2581184:back.name: Anthony Gill
2581184:back.note: Gill (back) is questionable for Wednesday against the Hawks.
2581184:back.long: Gill's availability is uncertain as Washington deals with multiple injuries in its frontcourt. Gill's status should become clearer closer to tipoff, though he remains a limited fantasy option even if cleared to play.

5149077:suspension.name: Kingston Flemings
5149077:suspension.note: Flemings (suspension) won't play in Monday's game against Indiana, Andrew Schlecht of The Athletic reports.
5149077:suspension.long: Flemings was assessed a technical foul and ejected late in the Hawks' 121-99 loss to New Orleans on Saturday for intentionally elbowing Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head. Without the rookie on the floor, head coach Quin Snyder will presumably divide the minutes between Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Aaron Wiggins and CJ McCollum.

3936099:knee.name: Derrick Jones Jr.
3936099:knee.note: Jones (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
3936099:knee.long: Jones exited Sunday's loss to the Warriors and did not return due to a right knee injury. He's now listed on the injury report with right knee soreness, and the veteran forward's next chance to play will come Wednesday against Miami. In the meantime, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased playing time.

3134908:shoulder.name: Jakob Poeltl
3134908:shoulder.note: Poeltl (shoulder) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Clippers, Zulfi Sheikh reports.
3134908:shoulder.long: Poeltl will now miss his second consecutive contest due to left shoulder bursitis. Collin Murray-Boyles and Tracye Jackson-Davis both stand to see increased playing time, with the latter the top candidate to earn a second straight start.

4251:rest.name: Paul George
4251:rest.note: George will be rested Monday against Houston.
4251:rest.long: There's no injury to report and this appears to be a planned maintenance day for the veteran. With George on the shelf, the Celtics will need guys like Payton Pritchard and Baylor Scheierman to absorb more minutes.

4397040:quadriceps.name: Brandon Williams
4397040:quadriceps.note: Williams (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Suns.
4397040:quadriceps.long: Williams will be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quad contusion. His next chance to play will come Thursday against Miami. Will Richard and De'Anthony Melton could see a bump in minutes in Williams' stead.

3213:rest.name: Al Horford
3213:rest.note: Horford will be rested Monday against the Suns.
3213:rest.long: As expected, Horford will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. Fortunately for the Warriors, Draymond Green (back) is set to return to the lineup.

2580365:illness.name: Larry Nance Jr.
2580365:illness.note: Nance (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hawks.
2580365:illness.long: Including Nance, the Pacers have ruled out 10 players ahead of Monday's contest. Kobe Brown and Jarace Walker should see heavy workloads with the club shorthanded.

4396909:rest.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:rest.note: Nesmith (rest) is sitting out Monday against Atlanta.
4396909:rest.long: The Pacers are holding him out for left hamstring injury management, but this is a maintenance day and not a setback for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Kelly Oubre and Jarace Walker could see hefty workloads with so many Pacers sitting out.

4395712:neck.name: Andrew Nembhard
4395712:neck.note: Nembhard (cervical strain) is out for Monday's game against Atlanta.
4395712:neck.long: The Pacers are going to sit multiple key players for the second leg of this back-to-back set. With Nembhard sidelined, Quenton Jackson could be set up for an extended workload.

3149673:rest.name: Pascal Siakam
3149673:rest.note: Siakam will be rested against the Hawks on Monday.
3149673:rest.long: The veteran forward compiled 17 points (6-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, five assists and a steal across 35 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 loss to the Nets, and he'll be held out for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Obi Toppin (lumbar sprain) is questionable, so the Pacers may need a lot of minutes from Jarace Walker.

4066648:quadriceps.name: Rui Hachimura
4066648:quadriceps.note: Hachimura (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
4066648:quadriceps.long: The 28-year-old forward will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quadriceps contusion, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Heat. With Hachimura and Derrick Jones both sidelined, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are all candidates for increased playing time, especially if Max Strus (foot) operates under a minutes restriction in his regular-season debut with the Clippers.

4432847:hip.name: Terrence Shannon Jr.
4432847:hip.note: Shannon (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
4432847:hip.long: Shannon will miss his first game of the season due to a left hip contusion, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against Houston. With the 26-year-old swingman joining Anthony Edwards (knee) on the inactive list, more minutes will be available for guys like Ayo Dosunmu, Isaiah Evans and Jaylen Clark.

4432816:wrist.name: LaMelo Ball
4432816:wrist.note: Ball is questionable for Monday's game against Milwaukee due to a right wrist contusion.
4432816:wrist.long: Ball's status is uncertain heading into Monday's matchup, leaving Minnesota's backcourt potentially shorthanded. With Anthony Edwards (knee) already ruled out, Ball's availability will be particularly important for the Timberwolves' offensive production. Bones Hyland and Ayo Dosunmu could be heavily involved if Ball is absent.

4712849:rest.name: Anthony Black
4712849:rest.note: Black will be rested Monday against the Wizards.
4712849:rest.long: The Magic are listing him out for left ankle injury management, so they are taking a cautious approach for the second leg of this back-to-back set. He finished with 23 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 10-11 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two steals over 33 minutes Sunday against Boston. Jase Richardson, Jevon Carter and Jamal Cain could be more involved as a result.

4433134:hip.name: Scottie Barnes
4433134:hip.note: Barnes (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Clippers.
4433134:hip.long: Barnes is dealing with left hip soreness and could miss the second leg of this back-to-back set. The star forward's absence would open up additional minutes for the likes of Collin Murray-Boyles, Jamison Battle and Allen Graves.

4432187:shoulder.name: Reece Beekman
4432187:shoulder.note: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
4432187:shoulder.long: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

4432582:hip.name: Max Christie
4432582:hip.note: Christie (hip) is out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
4432582:hip.long: The swingman is missing his first game of the season with a hip injury , which he suffered Monday against the Kings. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher stand out as the most likely candidates to step into the starting lineup Wednesday.

3133603:knee.name: Kelly Oubre Jr.
3133603:knee.note: Oubre (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hawks.
3133603:knee.long: Oubre is dealing with a bruised left knee and will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. The Pacers will be extremely shorthanded Monday, opening the door for Quenton Jackson and Jarace Walker to take on significant workloads.

4278355:coach-s-decision.name: Obi Toppin
4278355:coach-s-decision.note: Toppin (back) will dress for Monday's game against  Hawks but will only play in an emergency, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
4278355:coach-s-decision.long: Toppin has missed the last two games while dealing with a lumbar strain, and the only reason he's dressing Monday is in the event of an emergency, as the Pacers are down to eight active players (including Toppin). Jay Huff, Kelly Oubre, Kobe Brown, Jarace Walker and Jalen Slawson will be tasked with eating up minutes in the frontcourt with Toppin, Ivica Zubac (ankle) and Larry Nance (illness) sidelined.

4278402:calf.name: Jordan Goodwin
4278402:calf.note: Goodwin won't return to Monday's game against the Warriors due to a left calf injury, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports. He recorded four points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 10 minutes before exiting.
4278402:calf.long: Rasheer Fleming and Ryan Dunn could see more opportunities in the second half with Goodwin shut down for the evening. The severity of his injury is unclear at this time.

4066354:shoulder.name: Payton Pritchard
4066354:shoulder.note: Pritchard is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee due to a right shoulder contusion, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4066354:shoulder.long: Pritchard's status is uncertain after he struggled in Monday's loss to Houston, finishing with four points on 0-for-7 shooting across 30 minutes. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also questionable and Devin Carter (illness) ruled out, Boston could be shorthanded Wednesday. Pritchard's availability should become clearer closer to tipoff.

4065648:rest.name: Jayson Tatum
4065648:rest.note: Tatum (rest) is questionable for Wednesday against the Bucks, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4065648:rest.long: Tatum's questionable designation suggests Boston could give its star forward a night off for maintenance purposes. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Wednesday's tipoff, as his potential absence would open up additional scoring opportunities for the Celtics' remaining starters.

3062679:ankle.name: Josh Hart
3062679:ankle.note: Hart is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bulls due to right ankle soreness.
3062679:ankle.long: Hart sounds to be nursing a minor issue, and he could go through pregame warmups before the Knicks clarify his status. The door would open for either Landry Shamet and Miles McBride to enter the starting lineup if Harts sits out Wednesday.

4432823:back.name: Jaylin Williams
4432823:back.note: Williams (back) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
4432823:back.long: Williams is battling lower back spasms, so his availability for Wednesday's meeting with Cleveland is in jeopardy. There are a few different directions head coach Mark Daigneault can go regarding the rotation, but if Williams doesn't suit up, it would likely open up more minutes for Micah Peavy, Kenrich Williams and Aday Mara.

4277919:ankle.name: Mo Bamba
4277919:ankle.note: Bamba is questionable for Wednesday's game in New Orleans due to a sprained right ankle.
4277919:ankle.long: Bamba must have tweaked his ankle during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs, and now he's in danger of sitting out Wednesday's game. If Bamba is forced to the sidelines, Kyle Filipowski would likely pick up most of his minutes.

5209602:coach-s-decision.name: Matilde Villa
5209602:coach-s-decision.note: Villa (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against New York.
5209602:coach-s-decision.long: Villa signed with Atlanta on Sept. 15 but will end the campaign without having seen any game action. She's ineligible to play in the postseason while on a developmental pact.

3058895:leg.name: Brionna Jones
3058895:leg.note: Jones will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining a left leg injury against the Sun on Aug. 13, Annie Costabile of The Athletic reports.
3058895:leg.long: This is a tough blow for a Dream team that is sitting in second place in the Eastern Conference. Jones managed to play in just nine games this campaign, finishing with averages of 8.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists. Look for the Dream to use a committee approach to soak up those minutes going forward.

4066548:foot.name: DiJonai Carrington
4066548:foot.note: Carrington (foot) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Mystics.
4066548:foot.long: Carrington will end the season on the inactive list for a fifth consecutive contest due to a left foot injury. She'll finish the campaign having averaged 8.8 points, 3.1 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 0.6 steals in 16.2 minutes per game across 11 regular-season outings. She's set to enter unrestricted free agency this offseason following an injury-riddled year.

4433433:knee.name: Aicha Coulibaly
4433433:knee.note: Coulibaly (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics
4433433:knee.long: Coulibaly's rookie year comes to an end due to a knee injury. She'll be looking to take a step forward next year after averaging 5.2 points, 2.6 rebounds and 0.7 steals per game this year for the Sky.

3142010:knee.name: Azura Stevens
3142010:knee.note: Stevens (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics
3142010:knee.long: Steven is sidelined Thursday with a knee injury, ending her regular season. The veteran forward is under contract with the Sky for 2027, and she averaged 10.6 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks per game in 2026.

2529137:knee.name: Natasha Cloud
2529137:knee.note: Cloud (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics.
2529137:knee.long: Cloud is out for the season finale Thursday with a knee injury. The veteran guard is slated to be an unrestricted free agent this winter, having averaged 11.1 points, 4.8 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game for the Sky this year.

2491205:knee.name: Skylar Diggins
2491205:knee.note: Diggins (knee) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Sara Jane Gamelli of BallisLife.com reports.
2491205:knee.long: She will now "focus on recovering an aggravated right knee injury." She hadn't played since July 3 and her rehab didn't progress as quickly as she would've hoped. She appeared in 19 games and posted averages of 14.2 points, 3.2 rebounds and 4.9 assists.

4433630:knee.name: Rickea Jackson
4433630:knee.note: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.
4433630:knee.long: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.

4433792:knee.name: Rayah Marshall
4433792:knee.note: Marshall has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game against the Tempo due to a right knee injury.
4433792:knee.long: Marshall suffered a knee injury shortly after checking in and won't be able to continue in this one. Nell Angloma could see a few more minutes in Marshall's absence.

4398966:knee.name: Olivia Nelson-Ododa
4398966:knee.note: Nelson-Ododa (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
4398966:knee.long: Nelson-Ododa is sidelined for the regular-season finale with a knee injury. She has one more year left on her deal after averaging a career-high 10.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists for the Sun in 2026.

4433514:ankle.name: Saniya Rivers
4433514:ankle.note: Rivers (ankle) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
4433514:ankle.long: Rivers is missing the regular-season finale with an ankle injury. She's under contract for next year after averaging 6.9 points, 3.1 assists and 1.1 steals per game over 38 appearances in 2026.

2490553:knee.name: Brittney Griner
2490553:knee.note: Griner (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
2490553:knee.long: Griner is sitting out the regular-season finale due to a knee injury. The veteran center was limited to 18 appearances this year, and she's set for unrestricted free agency this offseason.

3922628:shoulder.name: Kennedy Burke
3922628:shoulder.note: The Sun announced Monday that Burke suffered a sprained AC joint in the FIBA World Cup and will miss the rest of the season.
3922628:shoulder.long: With Connecticut eliminated from playoff contention, Burke is sitting out the remaining four games on the schedule with an eye toward next season. Her absence should allow Nell Angloma and Aaliyah Edwards to handle more playing time. Burke averaged a career-high 8.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists per contest in 37 games this season.

3913881:lower-leg.name: Alanna Smith
3913881:lower-leg.note: Smith (lower leg) is out for Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs against Golden State on Friday.
3913881:lower-leg.long: Smith will miss the entirely of the first round while nursing a lower leg injury suffered during the FIBA World Cup. Maddy Siegrist and Alysha Clark will once again be asked to step up with Smith sidelined.

4433790:knee.name: Azzi Fudd
4433790:knee.note: Fudd will undergo an arthroscopic procedure to address her right knee soreness and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 season.
4433790:knee.long: Fudd has been sidelined since early August due to her ongoing right knee soreness, and she'll undergo a procedure that will ultimately end her rookie season. Across 30 regular-season appearances (24 starts) this year, she averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 31.7 minutes per game. In her absence, Odyssey Sims, Alanna Smith and Alysha Clark have seen increased roles, and that trend will likely continue down the stretch as the Wings compete for a playoff berth.

5345473:personal.name: Costanza Verona
5345473:personal.note: Verona's contract was temporarily suspended by the Wings Saturday.
5345473:personal.long: Verona is signed to a developmental contract, so she has only appeared in one regular-season game for Dallas during the 2026 campaign. She will now head overseas, where she will suit up for the Italian National Team for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. It's unknown whether Verona will be back with the Wings, though her departure will allow the team to sign another player to a developmental deal.

4790263:not-injury-related.name: Iliana Rupert
4790263:not-injury-related.note: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.
4790263:not-injury-related.long: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.

4065760:leg.name: Tyasha Harris
4065760:leg.note: Harris (leg) will miss the rest of the season, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.
4065760:leg.long: Harris was injured during Thursday's 86-66 win over Minnesota. She was diagnosed with a broken left fibula, though it's unknown if it will affect her heading into the 2027 campaign. The 28-year-old averaged a career-low 4.1 points along with 1.1 rebounds and 2.0 assists over 13.5 minutes per contest in 39 regular-season games, including four starts, in 2026. While Harris wasn't a consistent contributor for Indiana during the season, her absence could at least open the door for a little more involvement from Myisha Hines-Allen and Monique Billings.

4398776:leg.name: NaLyssa Smith
4398776:leg.note: The Aces announced Thursday that Smith will be sidelined for the rest of the season after suffering a non-contact left leg injury during Sunday's game versus the Tempo, per Chelsea Leite of TSN.
4398776:leg.long: It's a big blow for the defending-champion Aces ahead of the postseason. Smith started all 38 of her appearances for Las Vegas, so a spot in the first unit is now open. Brianna Turner appears to the most likely candidate to replace Smith in the starting lineup going forward.

5106170:coach-s-decision.name: Ndjakalenga Mwenentanda
5106170:coach-s-decision.note: Mwenentanda (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Golden State.
5106170:coach-s-decision.long: Mwenentanda has appeared in her team's last two games, but she'll be shut down for the Sparks' final game of the 2026 campaign. She played in seven games across stops in LA and Golden State this season.

4433808:coach-s-decision.name: Shyanne Sellers
4433808:coach-s-decision.note: Sellers (coach's decision) is out for Thursday's game against the Valkyries.
4433808:coach-s-decision.long: Sellers will take a seat for the season finale despite being left off the injury report initially. She appeared in two games for the Sparks after signing a developmental contract in late August.

4433404:ankle.name: Cameron Brink
4433404:ankle.note: Brink (ankle) is listed as out for Thursday's game against Golden State.
4433404:ankle.long: Brink missed the last two games but will now be sidelined for the Sparks' final game of the season. The 24-year-old averaged a career-best 9.5 points along with 5.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.8 blocks over 19.2 minutes per contest in 31 regular-season games, including one start, throughout the 2026 campaign.

4597509:ankle.name: Aaliyah Nye
4597509:ankle.note: Nye (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Golden State.
4597509:ankle.long: Nye will end the campaign with a third consecutive absence due to a left ankle injury. She'll finish the season having averaged 1.0 points in 2.8 minutes per contest across 20 regular-season outings between Los Angeles and Atlanta.

5278237:foot.name: Anastasiia Olairi Kosu
5278237:foot.note: Kosu (foot) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Game 2 of the first round of the playoffs against the Liberty.
5278237:foot.long: Kosu will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a right foot injury, though her absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation. If the Lynx manage to stave off elimination Tuesday, the 21-year-old's next opportunity to play will come in Game 3 on Thursday.

5208984:coach-s-decision.name: Elena Buenavida
5208984:coach-s-decision.note: Buenavida (coach's decision) is out for Thursday's game against the Fever.
5208984:coach-s-decision.long: Buenavida will take a seat for Thursday's regular-season finale after initially being left off the injury report. She hasn't made an appearance for the Lynx after inking a developmental contract Aug. 11.

4398589:not-injury-related.name: Elizabeth Balogun
4398589:not-injury-related.note: Balogun (not with team) is out for Wednesday's game against the Dream.
4398589:not-injury-related.long: Balogun remains away from the Liberty for the regular-season finale Wednesday. It's unknown if she'll report to the club at any point this postseason.

4698730:coach-s-decision.name: Kara Dunn
4698730:coach-s-decision.note: Dunn (coach's decision) is listed as out for Thursday's game against the Aces.
4698730:coach-s-decision.long: Dunn is signed to a developmental contract and is eligible to appear in up to 12 regular-season contests. She played in the Mercury's last four games, most recently amassing a career-high 11 points in Monday's 87-86 win over Dallas. However, the rookie won't suit up for Phoenix's final game of the year, so she will finish the 2026 campaign with averages of 6.5 points and 1.5 rebounds over 15.0 minutes in four regular-season games. Dunn also shot an efficient 57.1 percent from behind the arc.

3065570:lower-leg.name: Kelsey Plum
3065570:lower-leg.note: Plum (leg) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports.
3065570:lower-leg.long: Plum is still not feeling the effects of a lingering lower leg injury and will be shut down with the Mercury out of the playoffs. The star guard is set to become a free agent at the conclusion of the season. In five appearances with the Mercury, she averaged 15.8 points and 2.8 assists.

3906769:not-injury-related.name: Jovana Nogic
3906769:not-injury-related.note: Nogic (not injury related) intends to play professionally in Russia and won't return to Phoenix this season, Aya Abdeen of TheIXSports.com reports.
3906769:not-injury-related.long: Nogic had her contract temporarily suspended June 20 and will now be out for the remainder of the WNBA season, as she's slated to compete overseas in Russia with an eye on leading the Serbian national team in the EuroBasket 2027 qualifiers. The guard appeared in 16 games (seven starts) for Phoenix, averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 20.2 minutes per contest. With Nogic out of the fold for the foreseeable future, Alexa Held stands to continue benefiting from expanded opportunities in the backcourt.

4433690:back.name: Holly Winterburn
4433690:back.note: Winterburn (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Golden State.
4433690:back.long: Winterburn will be held out of Portland's season finale due to a back injury, and she'll finish the 2026 campaign having averaged 4.0 points, 1.8 assists and 1.4 rebounds across 11.2 minutes per game in 29 regular-season appearances (one start). She began the season on a developmental deal before being converted to a standard contract, and the 25-year-old guard is set to be an unrestricted free agent this season.

5209202:knee.name: Nyadiew Puoch
5209202:knee.note: Puoch (knee) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Golden State.
5209202:knee.long: Puoch won't be available for the Fire's final game of the 2026 campaign, marking just her second absence of the season. Without Puoch in the mix, Frieda Buhner and Amy Okonkwo could see more action.

5346554:knee.name: Teja Oblak
5346554:knee.note: Oblak (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Valkyries.
5346554:knee.long: Oblak will end the season on the inactive list for a fourth consecutive game due to a left knee injury. The 35-year-old guard made her WNBA debut this year and will finish the 2026 campaign with averages of 5.6 points, 3.2 assists, 1.6 rebounds, 0.8 triples and 0.7 steals while shooting 36.7 percent from downtown across 13.4 minutes per game in 29 regular-season appearances (one start).

4682797:personal.name: Luisa Geiselsoder
4682797:personal.note: Geiselsoder (personal) won't return this season, according to Sean Highkin of RoseGardenReport.com.
4682797:personal.long: Geiselsoder will represent Germany at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup, and since she's been out of the rotation for a while, she's leaving early for preparation and won't return this season. She ends the season with averages of 4.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 16.6 minutes per game in 21 appearances (nine starts).

4703794:knee.name: Sarah Ashlee Barker
4703794:knee.note: The Fire announced Friday that Barker will undergo surgery to repair a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
4703794:knee.long: Barker was helped to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Wings, and she's now been diagnosed with a season-ending injury. The second-year guard took on a significant role for the Fire after the club selected her in the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft. Across 26 regular-season games (15 starts), the 24-year-old averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest. Karlie Samuelson, Teja Oblak and Nyadiew Puoch are candidates for increased playing time in Barker's stead.

4433795:knee.name: Sania Feagin
4433795:knee.note: Feagin (knee) was diagnosed with a torn left ACL on Thursday and will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.
4433795:knee.long: Feagin agreed to a developmental contract with Portland on June 24 after spending time in Los Angeles. After appearing in 16 regular-season games for the Sparks in 2025, the 23-year-old played in only three regular-season contests in 2026, logging a combined 10 minutes. Feagin had yet to make her debut with the Fire, though that will now need to wait, assuming Portland keeps her on the roster moving ahead.

5106222:coach-s-decision.name: Taina Mair
5106222:coach-s-decision.note: Mair (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Wings.
5106222:coach-s-decision.long: Mair will sit out Seattle's season finale. The developmental player will finish her rookie season with averages of 1.3 points and 0.5 assists in 5.1 minutes per game across 10 regular-season outings.

4432832:knee.name: Zia Cooke
4432832:knee.note: Cooke (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
4432832:knee.long: Cooke will end the 2026 campaign with a third consecutive absence due to a right knee injury. She'll also finish the season having averaged career-high marks in points (7.5), rebounds (1.7) and assists (1.1) across 15.0 minutes per game in 41 regular-season appearances (one start). She's set to enter restricted free agency this offseason.

3917453:knee.name: Katie Lou Samuelson
3917453:knee.note: The Storm announced Friday that Samuelson underwent successful left knee surgery and will miss the remainder of the season.
3917453:knee.long: Seattle's frontcourt takes another hit after losing Ezi Magbegor to a torn ACL on Thursday. Samuelson had a delayed start to the year due ACL surgery recovery, averaging 4.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 15.3 minutes per contest over 32 games this season. The Storm should lean more heavily on Stefanie Dolson, Mackenzie Holmes and Taylor Thierry the rest of the way.

4398768:knee.name: Nyara Sabally
4398768:knee.note: Sabally recently underwent arthroscopic left knee surgery but is expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 season, Ian Finlayson of Sportsnet.ca reports.
4398768:knee.long: Sabally is coming off a career year with the Tempo, during which she averaged 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.9 blocks across 23.9 minutes per contest. However, she was limited by injuries, appearing in only 24 regular-season games (20 starts). She has already begun her rehab process and will be a restricted free agent this offseason.

5017605:coach-s-decision.name: Kamila Borkowska
5017605:coach-s-decision.note: Borkowska (coach's decision) is out for Thursday's game against the Sun.
5017605:coach-s-decision.long: Borkowska will be sidelined for her team's final matchup of the regular season. She didn't appear in a game for the Tempo after signing a developmental contract Saturday.

4898548:coach-s-decision.name: Maria Gakdeng
4898548:coach-s-decision.note: Gakdeng is out for Thursday's game against the Sun as a coach's decision.
4898548:coach-s-decision.long: Gakdeng's season is over before she was able to make her debut. She'll look for another developmental opportunity this offseason.

3910470:back.name: Maria Conde
3910470:back.note: Conde (back) is out for Thursday's game against the Sun.
3910470:back.long: Conde is sitting out the regular-season finale Thursday. The rookie forward is set to be a reserved free agent this winter but should receive a qualifying offer, having averaged 8.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game for Toronto in 2026.

2569044:personal.name: Temi Fagbenle
2569044:personal.note: Fagbenle (personal) is out for Thursday's game against the Sun.
2569044:personal.long: Fagbenle won't rejoin the team for the regular-season finale due to personal reasons. She's set for unrestricted free agency this offseason, having averaged 5.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.0 assists for the Tempo this year.

3904576:hip.name: Marina Mabrey
3904576:hip.note: Mabrey (hip) will miss the final four games of the 2026 season, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet reports.
3904576:hip.long: Mabrey, who has been sidelined since mid-August, will not require surgery and is expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 WNBA season. Across 32 appearances, she produced averages of 20.8 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 0.9 steals.

4684384:knee.name: Aneesah Morrow
4684384:knee.note: Morrow (knee) will miss the rest of the 2026 season, Chelsea Leite of TSN reports.
4684384:knee.long: Brittney Sykes (foot) will also miss the final eight games for Toronto. According to coach Sandy Brondello, Morrow is not facing a lengthy recovery. Kia Nurse and Ornella Bankole are candidates to step into larger roles the rest of the way.

2988756:foot.name: Brittney Sykes
2988756:foot.note: Sykes (foot) will miss the remainder of the 2026 season, Chelsea Leite of TSN reports.
2988756:foot.long: This is a tough blow for Toronto, but Sykes' foot issues have continued to linger. She will finish the campaign with averages of 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.5 blocks in 29.4 minutes per contest. Kia Nurse and Ornella Bankole could see larger roles the rest of the way with this news.
